productArtifacts.title: Datastreamer for Edge Hub OS logs
productArtifacts.body:
In Splunk OT Intelligence, open Data Ingestion and create a Datastreamer:
HEC hostname: the HTTP Event Collector URL of your Splunk platform deployment
HEC token: a token whose allowed indexes include the index below
Name: logs
Index: edge_hub_logs (events index)
Topics: edgehub/logs
Data Volume: Standard
Backlog Size: 100,000
Batch Size: 10
Source Type: _json

description: Detects Pipeline Health anomalies for UC-14.3.7 with window `the scheduled window` on `index=edge_hub_logs` sourcetype `_json`. Combines `count` by `priority` and compares against configured threshold. Mapped to keywords Edge, Cloud, Data, Pipeline, Health for dashboard routing.
value: Alerting on Edge, Cloud, Data, Pipeline, Health through UC-14.3.7 reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by surfacing `activity` early.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `edge_hub_logs` (UC-14.3.7)** — Planned work for 'Edge-to-Cloud Data Pipeline Health' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `priority` remains in-scope.  Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `_json`** — Scheduled automation elevates `src` without crossing configured threshold for UC-14.3.7. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `priority`** — Health checks in `edge_hub_logs` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `_json`** — First 48h baseline for UC-14.3.7 on `priority` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `priority`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Edge Hub (system health), Splunk OT Intelligence.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `index=edge_hub_logs` (Edge Hub OS system logs: hub_name, unit, message, boot_id, priority). Sent to HEC by a Splunk Edge Hub OS Datastreamer configured in Splunk OT Intelligence (Edge Hub OS does not support a universal forwarder).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Edge Hub streams device health data to `edge_hub_status` index and system logs to `edge_hub_logs` index. The device checks Splunk reachability every 15 seconds — LED ring shows green (connected) or red (disconnected). When disconnected, data backlogs locally: 3M sensor data points and 100K health/logs/anomalies/SNMP entries each (FIFO, batches of 100 via HEC on reconnect). Monitor CPU, memory, disk utilization on the device. Alert on connectivity loss or sustained high resource usage.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=edge_hub_logs
  ("connection" OR "unreachable" OR "timeout")
| timechart count by priority
```

Understanding this SPL

**Edge-to-Cloud Data Pipeline Health** — Edge Hub pipeline health ensures IoT/OT data reaches Splunk. A disconnected Edge Hub creates blind spots — the device backlogs up to 3M sensor data points locally in SQLite.

Documented **Data sources**: `index=edge_hub_logs` (Edge Hub OS system logs: hub_name, unit, message, boot_id, priority). Sent to HEC by a Splunk Edge Hub OS Datastreamer configured in Splunk OT Intelligence (Edge Hub OS does not support a universal forwarder). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Edge Hub (system health), Splunk OT Intelligence. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: edge_hub_logs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=edge_hub_logs. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `timechart` plots the metric over time with a separate series **by priority** — ideal for trending and alerting on this use case.

Step 3 — Validate
Confirm metric or event volume in the time range, then compare trends and device status to the Splunk Edge Hub admin UI or the mobile app for the same devices. Verify metric names, hosts, and time skew.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Single value (connectivity status with LED color mapping), Gauge (CPU/memory/disk), Line chart (forwarding rate over time).
